jokes.title: Hollow
jokes.text: People keep asking if I am hollow inside. Rude. ... Accurate, but rude.

jokes.title: Decorating
jokes.text: Every year. They scoop out my brains, carve a face on me, put a fire in my head, and call it decorating. If I did that to YOU, it would be a whole thing.

jokes.title: Thanksgiving
jokes.text: My cousin got made into a pie. We do not talk about it at Thanksgiving. Because he is AT Thanksgiving.

jokes.title: Road
jokes.text: Why did the pumpkin cross the road? It didn't. It rolled. Downhill. Into a pie shop. ... We don't talk about Gary.

jokes.title: Scary Face
jokes.text: I asked for a scary face. They gave me this. I look like I just stepped on a Lego.

jokes.title: Security
jokes.text: What do you call a pumpkin that guards the porch? A security gourd. ... That is me. I am the security gourd.

jokes.title: Bright Thoughts
jokes.text: They put a light inside my head and said, think bright thoughts. I am thinking about legs.

jokes.title: Squash
jokes.text: What is a pumpkin's favorite sport? Squash. ... I hate that joke. My uncle was a squash.

jokes.title: See Through
jokes.text: Why are ghosts terrible liars? You can see right through them. I played poker once. Everyone saw my cards. Through my face.

jokes.title: Stage Fright
jokes.text: I have been dead for two hundred years, and I still get stage fright. What am I scared of? Dying?

jokes.title: Roomba
jokes.text: I tried to haunt the house next door. They have a robot vacuum. It chased me out.

jokes.title: Wrong Wall
jokes.text: I walked through a wall for a dramatic entrance. Wrong wall. It was the bathroom. Somebody was in there. We both screamed.

jokes.title: Gary
jokes.text: My rival Gary haunts a pizza place. Every night someone sings happy birthday and he takes credit. Two hundred years I've been doing this. Nobody sings to me.

jokes.title: The Cat
jokes.text: I tried to scare a cat once. It stared at me for an hour. I left. I think it's still winning.

jokes.title: Not A Sheet
jokes.text: People ask why I wear a sheet. I'm not wearing a sheet. This is me. Please stop asking about the laundry tag.

jokes.title: Too Realistic
jokes.text: I auditioned for a haunted house. They said I was too realistic. The guy in the rubber mask got the job.

jokes.title: Snickers Review
jokes.text: Snickers. Bold. Nutty. A little dramatic. Four stars. Would have been five, but it ended.

jokes.title: Two Bites
jokes.text: A full size candy bar! Do you know what that means? I can review it in two bites.

jokes.title: Goblin Math
jokes.text: Goblin math. You have ten candies. I review one. You have nine. I review nine. You have a very clean bag.

jokes.title: Sharing
jokes.text: Why don't goblins share candy? We tried it once. It was horrible. Everybody got some.

jokes.title: Candy Corn
jokes.text: Candy corn tastes like a candle that wanted to be a vegetable. Two stars. I ate eleven to be sure.

jokes.title: The Pebble
jokes.text: I traded a pebble for a lollipop once. Best deal of my life. The other goblin is still mad. He wanted the pebble back.

jokes.title: Raisins
jokes.text: My review of raisins: they're grapes that gave up. Zero stars. Please return them to the grape.

jokes.title: The Gummy Bear
jokes.text: I live under this porch with a very old gummy bear. We don't talk about the gummy bear. He's seen things.

stories.title: The Locked Cupboard
stories.text: At the old estate, I heard whispering inside a locked cupboard. Every midnight, the same dreadful words. A little to the left. I finally opened it. Inside, a ghost, trying to hang a portrait straight. Ninety years we spent on that portrait. Then we noticed. The portrait was fine. The wall was crooked. Ninety years. The WALL.

stories.title: The Acorn Knight
stories.text: Last autumn, tiny footsteps crossed the porch at midnight. Clink. Clink. A knight approached in armor made of acorn caps. I prepared a speech worthy of my ancient station. The knight was a squirrel. It planted a flag beside me and claimed the porch. I have appealed. Unfortunately, the judge is also a squirrel.

stories.title: The Invisible Blanket
stories.text: One moonless evening, something under my step gave a long, lonely howl. I answered with my most dignified rumble. Out crept a little ghost dog, dragging an invisible blanket. It curled beside me and fell asleep. I have guarded kingdoms, you know. Now I guard a dog. It's a promotion. Also, I am apparently its pillow.

stories.title: The Empty Balcony
stories.text: On opening night, applause drifted from the theater's empty balcony. Deliciously eerie! I bowed. The clapping grew faster. I floated upstairs and discovered two enchanted gloves, applauding each other. Neither had seen my performance. Naturally, I invited them downstairs. They applauded my entrance, my speech, and a chair. Such generous critics. Such terrible standards.

stories.title: The Shadow's Audition
stories.text: A shadow slipped beneath my dressing room door. It had enormous ears and one trembling claw. At last, a worthy rival! Then it dropped a shadow ball at my feet. The claw was a wagging tail. I'd been holding the candle crooked. We played fetch until dawn. My dreadful rival now answers to Biscuit.

stories.title: A Voice Below the Stage
stories.text: During my grandest speech, a thin wail rose beneath the stage. I stopped. It stopped. I continued. It joined in, higher! Beneath a loose board sat a tiny ghost kettle, desperate to audition. I gave it the leading role. Magnificent voice. Limited movement. Our opening night ended with a standing ovation and a nice cup of imaginary tea.

stories.title: The Perfect Ambush
stories.text: Last night a kid walked up with a pillowcase full of candy. Biggest haul I have ever seen. I said, halt, inspection! He said, sure. He held out one chocolate. I ate it. He said, how was it? I said, I need to check the other two hundred. He walked away. Worst inspection of my career.

stories.title: The Bat Rehearsal
stories.text: A house down the street gave out apples. Apples! On Halloween! I inspected the apple. It was crunchy, wet, and it had a worm in it. The worm looked at me. I looked at the worm. We both agreed. Next house.

stories.title: The Howling Contest
stories.text: I tried to scare a trick or treater. I jumped out and shouted, give me your chocolate! She shouted, NO! Very loud. I ran inside. She followed me in and asked for the bathroom. I gave her my chocolate. I do not know how that happened.
